title: Relaxo Footwears Ltd-$ - 530517 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Relaxo's H1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 13.8% despite ~20%+ realisation hikes, with management saying margins stay under pressure, volumes keep dipping, and the company is cutting capacity-reliant mix rather than adding capex.

summary.headline: Relaxo Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11.6% to INR 702 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.2% as input and wage costs outran pricing.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 702 crore (up 11.6% YoY), with EBITDA up 5.1% to INR 85 crore and PAT up 2.2% to INR 37 crore. H1 FY27 revenue grew 9.6% to INR 1,407 crore, while EBITDA margin was 13.8% (H1) and PAT margin 6.5%. Management attributed margin pressure to West Asia-driven raw material volatility, statutory minimum wage hikes and brand/retail investments, and said margins will stay under pressure unless the conflict settles. Price increases of roughly 15-18% in open footwear and 6-7% in Sparx closed footwear drove realisations up over 20%, with volumes falling in mass slippers. The company also announced a Kenya JV (Relaxo Kenafric Footwears) for East Africa manufacturing.

financial_highlights.change: Largely pricing per analyst; management confirmed price-led

segments.name: General trade
segments.commentary: Steady momentum in H1 supported by distributor and retailer network; management expects growth next year after pricing is absorbed by trade, but it must be adjusted for price and volume.

segments.name: Retail (EBOs)
segments.commentary: Fastest-growing channel with at least 23% revenue growth; EBO count rose to 445 after 16 stores added in Q2, with 51 reimagined stores and a target of 500 by year-end. Management expects double-digit retail growth.

segments.name: E-commerce and modern trade
segments.commentary: Both contributed positively in H1 and are next in growth order after retail, per management.

segments.name: Open footwear (Hawaii, Flite, about 80% of sales)
segments.commentary: Open portfolio price increase of about 15-18%; Hawaii mass slippers show volume dip while Flite premium grew. Value growth in other open categories around 10%.

segments.name: Sparx (closed footwear)
segments.commentary: Roughly INR 1,000 crore revenue, with INR 500 crore from shoes; 6-7% price increase; shoes grew 18% in H1, targeted to reach double digit.

segments.name: Flite
segments.commentary: Roughly INR 1,000 crore revenue, similar to Sparx; premium Flite portfolio growing; ad campaign with Ali Fazal and Sanya Malhotra.

guidance_outlook: Management said margins will remain under pressure in H2 unless the West Asia conflict settles; no explicit guidance was reiterated on the 100 bps FY27 margin improvement, which an analyst queried.
Double-digit growth expected from Q4 FY27 onwards as price increases are absorbed by trade.
Expects summers to be better next year once raw material and labour cost pass-through is complete.
Targets 500 EBOs by year-end; plans 50 more reimagined stores in the next six months.
Kenya JV plant targeted to start in Q1 FY28 with capacity of about 50,000 pairs per day; no major capex needed for closed footwear growth.
capex_capacity: Kenya JV Relaxo Kenafric Footwears Ltd: total investment INR 70 crore, Relaxo holds 51% (up to INR 35.7 crore), making it a subsidiary; planned capacity about 50,000 pairs per day, start in FY28 Q1.
EBO network at 445 after 16 additions in Q2 FY27; target 500 by year-end.
Reimagined store format: 51 outlets (30 new) with similar square footage but more premium display; capex per store about INR 22 lakh.
Management said capacity is not reduced; optimised effective capacity from 10.5 to 9 reflects a shift to complex premium products that need more machine time.
Management said no major capex is required to grow closed footwear, as existing capacity is sufficient.
demand_pricing: Open footwear price increase of about 15-18%; Sparx closed footwear about 6-7%; around 150 new articles launched to soften consumer impact.
Hawaii mass slippers facing volume dip in a price-sensitive segment; value growth continues.

Industry context: BIS quality control covers about 10% of industry (exempt below INR 50 crore turnover); management says Chinese-origin product still enters via Bangladesh with no duty, and unorganised players are taking share.
Raw material volatility: rubber at INR 300/kg, described as the highest ever; management said Q3 is hard to call.
Management acknowledged it has not delivered the growth investors expected and said it is moving toward a consumer-centric, innovation-led model.

qa_highlights.question: Is ASP growth of 23% mostly pricing, and are pricing actions complete?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is price-led from raw material and labour costs; price increases have been taken across all categories, and further hikes are hard to predict. Increases were gradual, with about 150 new articles launched.

qa_highlights.question: Is steep pricing risking market share and volume loss, as in the past?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mass category (Hawaii) sees a volume dip, but value grew about 10% in other categories and sports/sneakers grew double digit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin dip despite the price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited indirect costs and wage increases outpacing top-line gains; revenue recognition has not changed.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Africa plan structured, and why local manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Local manufacturing in Kenya is meant to avoid import duty and port logistics issues; the plan starts with East Africa, with about 50,000 pairs per day capacity from FY28 Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin improvement guidance of 100 bps for FY27 hold?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cost increases are partly absorbed and partly passed on, so margins will be under pressure unless the war situation settles. Management did not reaffirm the 100 bps target.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital rise: what drove the 10-day increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days rose from 134 to 144 because expected volume growth did not materialise, plus inflation effects from 15-20% price increases.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin pressure from rubber and other raw material volatility plus wage inflation; H2 margin trajectory unclear.
Volume decline in mass slippers (Hawaii) and risk of share loss from steep pricing, a repeat of past volume declines.
Working capital days up to 144; monitor inventory build and receivables.
Competitive intensity from unorganised players, D2C brands, and Chinese-origin products entering via Bangladesh.
Execution of the 500-EBO target, reimagined store rollout and Kenya JV start in FY28 Q1; JV capital at risk until disclosed in detail.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic on growth drivers (retail, sports and sneakers) but candid about underperformance and margin pressure; the CFO was clear that margins will stay under pressure. Answers on margin guidance and BIS timing were less specific.
key_quotes: We recognize that we have not delivered the growth that investors expected over the last few years, and we are not satisfied with the performance either.
In future also, I am not seeing that unless the war situation is going to gets settled, the margins are going to be further under pressure.
We already have good capacities with us, so capex is not required that much to grow this category.

adds.what: Kenya JV Relaxo Kenafric Footwears East Africa plant, about 50,000 pairs/day (INR 70 crore total, Relaxo holds 51%)
EBO store network additions: 445 now, target 500 by year-end (about 55 more stores, ~INR 22 lakh capex per store)

growth.why: Management guided double-digit growth from Q4 FY27 and 500 EBOs by year-end (445 now), but cut the FY27 margin improvement view (no ~100bp reiterated) and says Q3 is hard to call; growth is mostly price-led with mass slipper volumes falling, and the Kenya JV (50,000 pairs/day) starts only in Q1 FY28.

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11.6% to INR 702 crore while realisations/ASP rose about 23% on 15-18% open-footwear and 6-7% Sparx price hikes, so growth is price-led with mass slippers volumes falling, and no one-off items were quantified in the brief.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin 13.8% and Q2 12.2% fell as raw material (rubber INR 300/kg) and wage costs outran pricing; management said margins stay under pressure in H2 unless West Asia conflict settles and did not reaffirm the ~100 bps FY27 improvement.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kenya JV plant (Relaxo 51% of INR 70 crore, ~50,000 pairs/day) targeted to start Q1 FY28, and EBOs go from 445 to 500 by year-end (about 55 stores at ~INR 22 lakh each), though the JV is a modest INR 35.7 crore of capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided double-digit growth from Q4 FY27 as price hikes of 15-18% (open) and 6-7% (Sparx) are absorbed, but Hawaii mass slipper volumes are dipping and H1 revenue growth was 9.6% with ASP up ~23%, so volume is not yet growing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said no major capex is needed for closed footwear growth as existing capacity is sufficient, and the only new capex is the small Kenya JV and EBO rollout (about INR 22 lakh per store).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management did not reaffirm the ~100 bps FY27 margin improvement and said Q3 is hard to call, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margins are under pressure in H2 with rubber at INR 300/kg (a record) and wage hikes, and the 100 bps FY27 margin view was not reiterated, so a margin guidance cut is a live risk if the West Asia conflict persists.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: About 150 new articles were launched to soften the price impact, and the premium Flite portfolio and sports/sneakers (double-digit growth) are the focus, though no specific named model launch was given.

rows.label: Kenya JV (Relaxo Kenafric) East Africa plant
rows.why: Relaxo holds 51% of INR 70 crore (INR 35.7 crore) for a ~50,000 pairs/day plant to avoid import duty and port logistics issues, with start guided for Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Retail EBO expansion to 500 stores
rows.why: EBOs at 445 after 16 added in Q2, with 51 reimagined stores and 50 more planned over six months; retail growing at least 23% and management expects double-digit retail growth.

rows.label: Inventory and working capital days reversal
rows.why: Inventory plus working capital days rose to 144 from 134 as expected volume growth did not come through, so release depends on volumes recovering from Q4 FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on retail, sports/sneakers and the Kenya JV but cautious on margins, saying H2 stays under pressure unless the West Asia conflict settles and not reaffirming the 100 bps FY27 target; analysts pressed on the margin guidance and on whether pricing will cost volume.
